To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the emission spectra were recorded and the number of emission spectral lines was determined for sealed carbon monoxide gas lasers filled with gas mixes containing 12C 16O, 12C16 O, and a mixture of 12C 1 6O and 13C 16O.
the emission spectrum of the CO laser filled with the mixture of isotopic compositions 12C16 O–13C16 O was shifted by 20 cm−1 in comparison with the spectrum of 12C16 0 and 13C16 0.

the emission spectra of sealed CO lasers were recorded for three isotopic compositions of CO at room temperature and the emission spectra of the lasers filled with 12CO and 13CO were shifted by 40cm−1 in the lower-frequency direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the isotopic composition of the gas on the spectral characteristics of CO lasers.
the spectral characteristics of sealed CO lasers with different isotopical compositions.
the development of new types of tunable lasers based on the use of the isotopic composition of the gas mixture as a parameter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spectral characteristics of sealed CO lasers with different isotopes of carbon and oxygen are similar, but there is a slight frequency shift of the laser spectrum in the case of the 13C16 isotope.
the 12C and 13C isotopes of CO are not equally efficient as lasing media.
the laser is a device which produces a beam of light that has a single frequency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spectral characteristics of the sealed carbon monoxide laser depend on the isotopic composition of the gas mixture.
the emission spectrum of the 13C16 laser is shifted by 40–45 cm−1 to the red compared with the spectrum from 12C16 laser.
the spectral characteristics of sealed lasers are determined by the isotopic composition of the active medium and are not affected by the isotopic purity of the laser gas mixture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a laser mixture containing two isotopic species can reduce the number of emission spectral lines.
the emission spectrum is determined mainly by the composition of the laser mixture and the resonator type.
the emission spectra of CO lasers with different isotopologues are similar, and the spectral range of emission is almost identical.
